items.prompt:
Some people think that university education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
In many countries, the cost of studying at university has risen sharply, and this has led to calls for higher education to be provided free of charge. While I accept that free tuition has clear benefits, I do not believe it should be available to every student without conditions.

There are strong arguments in favour of free university education. Firstly, it gives talented young people from poorer families the same opportunities as those from wealthy backgrounds. When fees are high, many capable students decide not to apply because they fear years of debt. Secondly, a well-educated population benefits the whole of society, not just individual graduates. Countries need doctors, engineers and teachers, and removing financial barriers helps to produce them.

However, making university completely free for everyone has significant drawbacks. Universities are expensive to run, and if students pay nothing, the cost must be met by taxpayers, including many people who never attended university themselves. In addition, when something is free, it may be valued less. Some students might enrol without a clear purpose, drop out after a year or take much longer than necessary to complete their degrees, wasting public money.

In my view, a more balanced approach would be to offer free or heavily reduced tuition to students who need financial support or who achieve high grades, while those who can afford to contribute pay at least part of the cost. Scholarship systems such as those offered in Saudi Arabia show how public funding can be targeted at able students and at subjects the country needs.

In conclusion, although free university education can increase fairness, I believe that support should be directed at those who need it most rather than given to all students regardless of their circumstances.

position.ar: يوافق الكاتب جزئيًا: التعليم المجاني مفيد، لكن يجب أن يُوجَّه لمن يحتاجونه أو للمتفوقين لا للجميع.
position.en: Partly agree: free tuition is valuable but should be targeted at those in need or high achievers, not everyone.

body: Benefits: equal opportunity; society needs graduates
Drawbacks: cost to taxpayers; less valued, wasted money
Own solution: targeted support and scholarships
outline.conclusion: Restate: support those who need it most

against: some students waste time and money

plan.ar: في أسئلة «إلى أي مدى توافق» حدّد موقفك بوضوح في المقدمة واحتفظ به حتى الخاتمة. يمكن أن يكون الموقف جزئيًا، لكن يجب أن يكون واضحًا.
plan.en: State your position clearly in the introduction and keep it consistent. A partial position is fine if it is clear.

items.prompt:
Some people believe that children should be allowed to use smartphones from a young age, while others think they should not have one until they are teenagers. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
Smartphones have become part of everyday life, and parents increasingly have to decide when their children should have one. Some argue that early access is useful, whereas others believe children should wait until their teenage years. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I support the second.

On the one hand, there are reasons why parents might give a phone to a young child. The most common is safety: a child with a phone can contact their parents if they are lost or in trouble, and parents can check where they are. Moreover, smartphones offer educational apps and games that can help children learn languages, mathematics and other skills. Some people also argue that because technology will play a central role in children’s future careers, they should become familiar with it as early as possible.

On the other hand, many experts warn that smartphones can harm young children. Time spent on screens often replaces physical activity, outdoor play and face-to-face conversation, all of which are essential for healthy development. Many apps are deliberately designed to keep users looking at them for as long as possible, and young children are less able to control how long they spend online. There is also the risk that they will see inappropriate content or be contacted by strangers.

In my opinion, the risks for young children outweigh the benefits. The safety argument can be met with a simple phone that only makes calls, and educational content can be accessed on a family computer under adult supervision. When children reach their teenage years, they are more mature and better able to use a smartphone responsibly, especially if their parents set clear rules.

In conclusion, although smartphones offer some advantages, I believe children should not have their own until they are teenagers.

position.ar: يؤيد الكاتب تأجيل الهاتف الذكي حتى سن المراهقة.
position.en: Children should wait until their teens.

body: View 1: safety, education, future skills
View 2: replaces play, addictive design, online risks
Opinion: simple phones and supervised computers meet the needs

plan.ar: في أسئلة «ناقش الرأيين» خصص فقرة لكل رأي بإنصاف، ثم صرّح برأيك (في المقدمة والخاتمة، أو في فقرة ثالثة).
plan.en: Give each view a fair paragraph, then state your own opinion clearly (intro and conclusion, or a third paragraph).

items.prompt:
In many cities, traffic congestion is becoming a serious problem. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
Traffic congestion has become a daily frustration for millions of people living in large cities. Long journeys waste time, increase pollution and harm the economy. This essay will examine the main causes of the problem and suggest some possible solutions.

The most obvious cause of congestion is the rapid growth in the number of private cars. As incomes rise, more families can afford a car, and many own two or three. In hot climates, cars are also seen as the only comfortable way to travel, so people use them even for very short journeys. A second cause is the way many modern cities have been planned. Homes, offices and shopping centres are often far apart, and public transport has not developed at the same speed as the cities themselves, which leaves residents with little choice but to drive.

Several measures could help to reduce congestion. The most effective long-term solution is to invest in fast, reliable and affordable public transport. Metro systems, such as the one recently opened in Riyadh, can carry far more people than roads and provide a real alternative to the car, especially if stations are well connected to bus services. Governments can also discourage unnecessary driving, for example by introducing charges for entering city centres at peak times or by raising parking fees.

In addition, employers have a role to play. Allowing staff to work from home on some days, or to start and finish at different times, would spread traffic more evenly throughout the day. Finally, future city planning should place homes closer to workplaces and services, so that journeys become shorter.

In conclusion, congestion is caused mainly by rising car ownership and poor urban planning. A combination of better public transport, financial incentives and flexible working could make a significant difference.

position.ar: الأسباب: زيادة السيارات وسوء التخطيط. الحلول: نقل عام قوي، رسوم ازدحام، مرونة العمل، تخطيط أفضل.
position.en: Causes: more cars, poor planning. Solutions: public transport, charges, flexible work, better planning.

outline.intro: Introduce the problem and essay plan
body: Causes: car ownership; city planning
Solutions: public transport; charges
Solutions: employers; future planning

plan.ar: أسئلة «الأسباب والحلول»: فقرة للأسباب (سببان مع شرح ومثال) وفقرة أو فقرتان للحلول المرتبطة بهذه الأسباب.
plan.en: One paragraph for causes (two, explained), one or two for solutions linked to those causes.

items.prompt:
More and more people are working from home rather than in an office. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
In recent years, advances in technology have made it possible for many employees to do their jobs from home. Although this trend has some drawbacks, I believe that its advantages are greater, provided that it is managed sensibly.

The benefits of working from home are considerable. The most obvious is the time saved by not commuting. Employees who used to spend two hours a day in traffic can use that time to rest, exercise or be with their families, which often leads to greater job satisfaction. Remote working also gives people more control over their schedules, which is particularly valuable for parents of young children. For companies, there are financial benefits too: they can reduce the cost of renting large offices and recruit talented staff who live in other cities.

Nevertheless, working from home is not without problems. Many people feel isolated when they rarely see their colleagues, and the casual conversations that happen in an office, which often produce new ideas, are difficult to replace online. New employees in particular may find it harder to learn from more experienced staff. In addition, the boundary between work and home life can become unclear, so some people end up working longer hours than before.

In my view, these disadvantages can largely be overcome. Many organisations now use a hybrid model, in which staff work in the office on two or three days a week and at home for the rest. This allows teams to meet regularly and new employees to receive support, while still giving workers the flexibility they value. Clear rules about working hours can also protect employees from burnout.

In conclusion, while remote working can lead to isolation and longer hours, the benefits in terms of time, flexibility and cost outweigh these problems, especially when a hybrid approach is adopted.

position.ar: المزايا أكبر، خاصة مع نموذج العمل الهجين.
position.en: Advantages outweigh disadvantages, especially with a hybrid model.

body: Advantages: no commute, flexibility, lower costs
Disadvantages: isolation, learning, blurred boundaries
Why the disadvantages can be overcome: hybrid model

vocab.en: the boundary between work and home

plan.ar: سؤال «هل تفوق المزايا العيوب؟» يتطلب حكمًا واضحًا. اعرض الجانبين ثم بيّن لماذا يرجح جانب على الآخر.
plan.en: “Do the advantages outweigh…” requires a clear verdict. Present both sides and explain why one is stronger.

items.prompt:
Some people say that the best way to protect the environment is for individuals to change their behaviour, while others believe that only governments and large companies can make a real difference. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
Environmental problems such as climate change and plastic pollution are among the greatest challenges facing the world. There is disagreement, however, about who is mainly responsible for solving them. In my opinion, while individuals have an important role, governments and large companies have far greater power to bring about change.

Those who emphasise individual action argue that every environmental problem is ultimately the result of millions of personal choices. If people drove less, used less electricity, avoided single-use plastic and wasted less food, the total effect would be enormous. Furthermore, consumer behaviour influences companies: when customers demand environmentally friendly products, businesses respond by producing them.

On the other hand, there are clear limits to what individuals can achieve. Many people want to live more sustainably but have no realistic alternatives. A person cannot take the train to work if there is no railway, and cannot avoid plastic packaging if almost every product in the supermarket is wrapped in it. Moreover, a large proportion of pollution comes from industry, energy production and transport systems, which are controlled by governments and corporations rather than ordinary citizens.

For these reasons, I believe that governments and large companies must lead. Governments can pass laws that limit emissions, invest in renewable energy and public transport, and use taxes to make polluting activities more expensive. Large companies can redesign their products and supply chains, which affects millions of customers at once. Individual efforts are still valuable, but they are most effective when the system makes the environmentally friendly choice the easiest one.

In conclusion, although personal behaviour matters, real progress depends mainly on action by governments and businesses, which can change the conditions in which individuals make their choices.

position.ar: الحكومات والشركات الكبرى أقدر على التغيير، مع بقاء دور الأفراد مهمًا.
position.en: Governments and companies must lead; individuals still matter.

body: Individual view: total effect, consumer influence
Limits of individuals: no alternatives, industry pollution
Why governments/companies must lead

against: laws and investment have bigger effects

plan.ar: حتى لو كان رأيك مع طرف، اعرض الطرف الآخر بعدل ثم بيّن حدوده.
plan.en: Even if you favour one side, present the other fairly and then show its limits.

items.prompt:
Nowadays many people choose to live alone. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
In many parts of the world, the number of people who live on their own has grown significantly in recent decades. This essay will consider the reasons for this trend and argue that, although it has some benefits, it is a largely negative development.

There are several reasons why more people are living alone. Firstly, rising incomes mean that more young adults can afford to rent their own homes rather than share with family or friends. Secondly, people are marrying later than in the past, often because they spend longer in education and building their careers, so many spend several years living independently. Finally, in some societies, people are living longer, and older people who lose their partners often continue to live alone in their own homes.

Living alone does have certain advantages. It gives people privacy and freedom to organise their lives as they wish, and it can help young adults become more responsible and independent. For some, it is a period of personal growth before they start a family.

Nevertheless, I believe the disadvantages are more serious. Loneliness is a growing problem, and research suggests that social isolation can damage both mental and physical health. Elderly people living alone may have no one to help them if they fall ill. There are also economic and environmental costs: single-person households use more energy, space and resources per person than larger households, which puts pressure on housing in crowded cities. In cultures such as my own, where extended families have traditionally lived close together, this trend may also weaken family ties.

In conclusion, more people live alone because of higher incomes, later marriage and longer lives. While independence has value, the risks of loneliness and the wider social costs make this a mainly negative development.

position.ar: الأسباب: الدخل، تأخر الزواج، طول العمر. الحكم: تطور سلبي في الغالب.
position.en: Causes: income, later marriage, longer lives. Mainly negative.

body: Reasons: income, later marriage, ageing
Some advantages: privacy, independence
Disadvantages: loneliness, cost, weaker family ties

plan.ar: الأسئلة ذات الجزأين: أجب عن السؤالين كليهما بوضوح وبالتساوي تقريبًا. كثير من الطلاب يخسرون درجة Task Response لأنهم يجيبون عن جزء واحد.
plan.en: Answer both questions fully. Many candidates lose Task Response marks by answering only one.

items.prompt:
Some people believe that governments should tax unhealthy foods such as sugary drinks and fast food in order to improve public health. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
Rates of obesity and diet-related illnesses such as diabetes have risen dramatically in many countries. As a result, some governments have introduced taxes on unhealthy products. I largely agree that such taxes are a sensible measure, although they should be combined with other policies.

The main argument for taxing unhealthy food is that price strongly influences what people buy. When sugary drinks become more expensive, many consumers choose cheaper alternatives such as water. Several countries, including Saudi Arabia, have introduced taxes on sweetened drinks, and in some places consumption has fallen as a result. In addition, the money raised can be used to fund health education or to make healthy food cheaper, so the tax produces a double benefit.

Furthermore, unhealthy diets do not only affect individuals. Treating illnesses linked to poor diet places a heavy burden on public health systems, which are paid for by everyone. It therefore seems fair that products which contribute to these costs should be taxed, in the same way that tobacco is.

There are, however, some valid objections. Critics argue that such taxes affect poorer families most, since they spend a larger share of their income on food. Others believe that adults should be free to choose what they eat without government interference. These concerns are understandable, but they can be addressed by using the revenue to reduce the price of fruit and vegetables, which would particularly help low-income households.

Nevertheless, taxation alone will not solve the problem. People also need to understand the effects of their diet, and children should learn about nutrition at school. Clear food labelling and limits on advertising to children are also important.

In conclusion, I believe that taxing unhealthy food is an effective way to improve public health, particularly as part of a wider strategy that includes education and support for healthy choices.

position.ar: يوافق إلى حد كبير، بشرط دمج الضريبة مع سياسات أخرى.
position.en: Largely agree, combined with other policies.

body: Price changes behaviour; revenue funds health
Costs to public health systems
Objections and answers
Tax alone is not enough

plan.ar: يمكن أن تكون المقالة بخمس فقرات إذا كانت الأفكار مترابطة. اذكر الاعتراض ثم رُدّ عليه (concession and refutation) لرفع درجة التماسك.
plan.en: Five paragraphs are fine. Mention objections and answer them (concession and refutation).

items.prompt:
Some people think that international tourism helps to protect local cultures, while others believe it damages them. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
International tourism has grown enormously, bringing millions of visitors to places that once received very few. Opinions differ as to whether this helps or harms the cultures of the places they visit. In my view, tourism can protect local traditions, but only if it is carefully managed.

Those who believe tourism protects local culture point first to its economic impact. When visitors are willing to pay to see traditional crafts, music or architecture, these traditions gain economic value, and young people have a reason to learn them rather than abandon them. Income from tourism can also be used to restore historic buildings and sites. The careful restoration of heritage areas in several Gulf cities, for example, has been supported partly by the expectation of visitors.

On the other hand, critics argue that tourism often damages the very cultures it claims to celebrate. Traditions may be turned into shows performed for visitors, losing their original meaning. Local shops may be replaced by international chains and souvenir stalls selling mass-produced goods. In popular destinations, large numbers of tourists can also make daily life difficult for residents and push up the cost of housing, forcing local people to move away.

I believe both views are valid, and that the outcome depends on how tourism is managed. Where local communities are involved in decisions and benefit directly from visitors, tourism can give them both the money and the pride needed to keep their traditions alive. Where it is driven only by profit, with little control over visitor numbers or development, the damage described by critics becomes more likely.

In conclusion, tourism is neither good nor bad for local culture in itself. With responsible planning and community involvement, its benefits can outweigh its risks.

position.ar: التأثير يعتمد على إدارة السياحة؛ مع الإدارة الجيدة تفوق المنافع المخاطر.
position.en: It depends on management; with good planning benefits outweigh risks.

body: Protects: economic value of traditions, restoration
Damages: shows, chains, crowding and housing costs
Opinion: depends on management and community involvement

plan.ar: يمكن أن يكون رأيك «يعتمد على…» بشرط أن تشرح بدقة متى يكون إيجابيًا ومتى يكون سلبيًا.
plan.en: An “it depends” opinion is fine if you explain exactly when each outcome happens.

items.prompt:
In many countries, a large amount of food is wasted by households and shops. What are the causes of this problem, and what can be done to reduce it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
In many countries, a surprisingly large proportion of the food that is produced never gets eaten. This essay will examine why so much food is thrown away by households and retailers, and suggest some practical measures to address the problem.

There are several reasons for this waste. In the home, people often buy more than they need, partly because supermarkets encourage bulk purchases through special offers such as ‘buy one, get one free’. Many consumers also misunderstand date labels and discard food marked ‘best before’ even though it is still perfectly safe to eat. In shops, the problem is largely driven by appearance: fruit and vegetables that are misshapen or slightly marked are frequently rejected because retailers believe customers will not buy them. Finally, in some cultures, generous hospitality means preparing far more food than guests can eat, and leftovers are rarely kept.

Fortunately, a combination of approaches could reduce this waste considerably. Governments could require supermarkets to donate unsold but edible food to charities instead of sending it to landfill, as France has done since 2016. Clearer labelling would also help: if packaging explained that ‘best before’ refers to quality rather than safety, fewer families would throw away good food. At the individual level, public awareness campaigns could encourage people to plan meals, write shopping lists and freeze leftovers. Restaurants and hotels, meanwhile, could offer smaller portions or allow diners to take uneaten food home.

In conclusion, food is wasted mainly because of over-buying, confusion over date labels and the high cosmetic standards of retailers. Laws on donating surplus food, clearer labels and campaigns to change consumer habits would all go a long way towards tackling this costly and avoidable problem.

position.ar: الأسباب: الشراء الزائد، وسوء فهم تواريخ الصلاحية، ومعايير المظهر في المتاجر، والإسراف في الضيافة. الحلول: إلزام المتاجر بالتبرع، وملصقات أوضح، وحملات توعية، وحصص أصغر في المطاعم.
position.en: Causes: over-buying, confusing date labels, cosmetic standards, over-generous hospitality. Solutions: compulsory donation, clearer labels, awareness campaigns, smaller portions.

outline.intro: Background + what the essay will do (causes and solutions)
body: Causes: special offers and over-buying; ‘best before’ confusion; rejected ‘ugly’ produce; hospitality
Solutions: donation laws (France); clearer labels; meal planning campaigns; smaller portions
outline.conclusion: Summarise the main causes and solutions

against: laws requiring donation of surplus food

plan.ar: في أسئلة المشكلة والحل خصّص فقرة للأسباب وفقرة للحلول، واجعل كل حل يعالج سببًا ذكرته. مثال واقعي واحد (قانون فرنسا) يقوّي الحجة.
plan.en: Give one paragraph to causes and one to solutions, and make each solution answer a cause you mentioned. One real example (France’s law) strengthens the argument.

items.prompt:
In some countries, more and more young people are taking a gap year — a year spent travelling, volunteering or working — between finishing school and starting university. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
In recent years, it has become increasingly common for school leavers to spend a year travelling, volunteering or working before they begin university. Although this ‘gap year’ carries certain risks, I believe that its benefits generally outweigh its drawbacks.

The most significant advantage is the personal development that a gap year can offer. Living away from home, managing a budget and dealing with unfamiliar situations force young people to become more independent and self-confident. A student who has spent several months volunteering abroad, for example, is likely to return with a clearer sense of what he or she wants to study. This can reduce the number of students who drop out or change courses in their first year, which is costly for both families and universities. In addition, work experience gained during the year can make graduates more attractive to employers later on.

There are, admittedly, some disadvantages. A gap year can be expensive, particularly if it involves international travel, so it is not equally available to students from less wealthy families. There is also a danger that some young people lose the habit of studying and find it difficult to return to academic work, while others may simply waste the year if it is not properly planned.

However, these problems can largely be avoided. Many gap-year activities, such as working locally or volunteering in one’s own country, cost little or even generate income, and a structured plan with clear goals keeps students focused. With careful preparation, the risk of wasting time is small compared with the long-term gains.

In conclusion, while a gap year may be costly and can disrupt study habits, the maturity, sense of direction and experience it provides make it, on balance, a worthwhile choice for most young people.

position.ar: المزايا تفوق العيوب: النضج والاستقلال ووضوح التخصص والخبرة العملية، أما التكلفة وفقدان عادة الدراسة فيمكن تجنبهما بالتخطيط.
position.en: Advantages outweigh disadvantages: maturity, direction and experience; cost and lost study habits can be managed with planning.

body: Advantages: independence; clearer choice of subject, fewer drop-outs; work experience
Disadvantages: cost and unequal access; losing study habits; wasted year
Why the disadvantages can be managed: local options, a structured plan

against: a wasted year without a plan

plan.ar: سؤال «هل تفوق المزايا العيوب؟» يطلب حكمًا واضحًا في المقدمة. اعرض الطرفين، ثم بيّن لماذا يرجح أحدهما (هنا: العيوب يمكن تجنبها).
plan.en: “Do the advantages outweigh…?” needs a clear verdict in the introduction. Cover both sides, then show why one side wins (here: the drawbacks can be avoided).

items.prompt:
Nowadays many people get their news from social media rather than from newspapers or television. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
items.model:
These days, a growing number of people, especially the young, rely on social media rather than traditional newspapers or television for their news. This essay will explain why this shift has occurred and argue that, despite some benefits, it is largely a negative development.

The main reason for this change is convenience. Almost everyone carries a smartphone, so news is available instantly, wherever people are, and usually free of charge. Social media also presents stories in short, visual formats such as videos and images, which suit busy lifestyles better than a long newspaper article or a fixed evening broadcast. Furthermore, these platforms allow users to follow the specific topics and people they care about, so the news they receive feels more personal and relevant.

This trend does have advantages. Urgent news, such as warnings about severe weather, can reach millions of people within minutes, and ordinary citizens can share eyewitness accounts of events that professional journalists might not cover.

Nevertheless, I believe the drawbacks are more serious. Unlike newspapers and broadcasters, which employ editors to check facts, social media allows anyone to publish anything, and false or misleading stories often spread faster than accurate ones. In addition, platforms use algorithms that show users content similar to what they have already liked, which can trap people in ‘echo chambers’ where they rarely encounter opposing views. Over time, this may make societies more divided. Finally, as advertising money moves to online platforms, many traditional news organisations have lost revenue, which reduces their ability to fund serious investigative journalism.

In conclusion, people increasingly turn to social media for news because it is fast, free and personalised. However, the spread of misinformation, the narrowing of perspectives and the decline of professional journalism make this a mainly negative development.

position.ar: الأسباب: السهولة والمجانية والصيغ القصيرة والتخصيص. الحكم: تطور سلبي في الغالب بسبب التضليل وغرف الصدى وتراجع الصحافة المهنية.
position.en: Causes: convenience, cost, short formats, personalisation. Mainly negative: misinformation, echo chambers, decline of professional journalism.

body: Reasons: smartphones and free access; short visual formats; personalised feeds
Some advantages: speed in emergencies; eyewitness reports
Disadvantages: no fact-checking; echo chambers; less funding for journalism

vocab.ar: غرفة الصدى (لا يسمع المرء إلا ما يوافقه)

plan.ar: السؤالان يحتاجان إجابة واضحة: فقرة للأسباب، ثم حكمك (إيجابي أم سلبي) مع ذكر الجانب الآخر باختصار. كرر الإجابتين في الخاتمة.
plan.en: Answer both questions clearly: a paragraph of reasons, then your verdict (positive or negative) with a brief look at the other side. Repeat both answers in the conclusion.
